title: Replay / Time-Travel Debugger (Fork tau): the DAG as a verified time machine
hypothesis: Because the engine is deterministic and content-addressed, history is event-sourced: a COMMAND LOG (the deterministic inputs that drove each phase change) plus SPARSE CHECKPOINTS (full MuState every K transitions) reconstruct ANY historical mu by restoring the nearest checkpoint and replaying commands forward. Replay is VERIFIED, not trusted: each reconstructed step's engine H_t must equal the recorded H_t -- a match is cryptographic proof of determinism and an un-tampered history; a mismatch raises ReplayMismatch. This turns EXP-518 BeyondWindowError into a COLD RESTORE and makes 'the past' a reproducible mathematical coordinate. Engine FROZEN.

mechanism.capture: step() journals {seq, inputs(beta_Z,strain,vort,N), result_H, child_id}; checkpoint every K.
mechanism.reconstruct: seq=h_index[H]; restore checkpoints[<=seq]; replay commands; assert step H==recorded H.
mechanism.cold_restore: reconstruct(H) for a target outside the skeleton undo window (Fork upsilon bridge).

engine_scope: NO engine edits. game/agency/replay.py uses core (MuState/Claim) + game.injection. state/operators/confluence/validity FROZEN.

[3] reconstruct(mid H) -> mu.H == target (exact historical reconstruction)
[4] verified replay: verify_history reproduces every recorded H (end-to-end determinism)
[5] checkpoint efficiency: reconstruct replays from nearest checkpoint (steps_replayed < target_seq)
[6] reconstruct genesis -> root mu; reconstruct latest -> live mu
[7] tamper detection: corrupt a recorded result_H -> ReplayMismatch
[8] COLD RESTORE: a CompactingWorld beyond its skeleton window -> cold_restore reconstructs the unreachable H
[9] reconstruct by int seq and by H string agree
